source_claims.statement: Extends desync beyond reverse-proxy front-ends by using the victim's browser as delivery platform. Combines cross-domain requests with server flaws to poison connection pools, install backdoors, release desync worms. Targets include Apache, Akamai, Varnish, Amazon, web VPNs.

research_questions.formulation: Can browser-sent cross-domain requests be used to deliver desync attacks against single-server targets and internal networks that lack an attacker-accessible reverse proxy?
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether desync is limited to attacker-controlled front-ends
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that desync requires an attacker-accessible reverse proxy

environment_model_updates: Browser connection pools can be poisoned
Cross-domain requests can carry desync payloads
